quotes.text: White shows the rye, the big of big of blaker hue,[…]
quotes.reference: 1747, Josiah Relph, A Miscellany of Poems,: Consisting of Original Poems, Translations, Pastorals in the Cumberland Dialect, Familiar Epistles, Fables, Songs, and Epigrams, page 13:

quotes.text: […] the E. blake (identical with AS. blac, G. bleich, pale) is provincially used in the sense of yellow. As blake as a paigle, as yellow as a cowslip.
quotes.reference: 1859, Hensleigh Wedgwood, A Dictionary of English Etymology: A - D, page 184:

quotes.text: Miss Lizzie's ower dark for my fancy. I mind nowt aboot your dark lasses - as blake as marygowds an' as black as corbies.
quotes.reference: 1876, Elizabeth Lynn Linton, Lizzie Lorton of Greyrigg: A Novel ..., page 271:

quotes.text: Noo, that's a bit o' neyce blake butter. Thoo nobbut leeaks blakeish.
quotes.reference: 1911, Richard Blakeborough, Wit, Character, Folklore & Customs of the North Riding of Yorkshire, page 340:
